NTE.NoteText:
From note

25kg/3 days
there are 2 cycles/year and 5 months/cycle
assume pigs stayed on farm for 300 days/year
Need: 25*300/3=2500 kg/year
DM weight= 2500*0.86=2150 kg
Cost=16400*2150=41,000,000 

The cost is higher than the value mentioned in survey (30,000,000)
Try to decrease cost for purchasing maize grain.
NTE.Name: CropProduct.3202

NTE.NoteText:
From note:
He buys 10 000 kg of maize grain at 6000 d/kg in one year and 2000 kg is for chicken. But there is no chicken in survey. 

From survey:
He spent 30,000,000 d/year on maize grain. Purchasing amount would be 5000 kg /year. 

Choose to use the data from survey. 
But since the cost for industrial feed is higher than the value mentioned in the survey. Try to decrease the cost spent on maize grain to compensate. 

In total they spent 60,000,000/year on industrial feed and maize grain.
Based on the NOTE, they spend 41,000,000 on industrial feed. They can only purchased 19,000,000 d of maize grain. 
Use 6,000 d/kg as the price of maize grain, they can pruchased = 19,000,000 / 6000 =31,666.6667 kg

But it's not enough for non-rumonats (energy)
Increase the amount to 3500 kg

ActiveOM.Explanation: Active organic matter content, the fraction of soil organic matter that is subject to mineralisation

OmDegradationRate.Explanation: Fraction of soil organic matter degraded

SoilDepth.Explanation: Depth of the soil profile considered for SOM breakdown

BulkDensity.Explanation: Bulk density of the soil profile

TextureFactor.Explanation: Texture factor influences the mineralisation of soil organic matter. Take a value of 1.2 for sandy soils, 1.0 for loam and 0.8 for clay.

SoilpH.Explanation: Soil pH. The pH-value of the soil influences the availability of minerals, the activity of soil organisms (and mineralisation), and the soil structure.

MoistPeriodPf35.Explanation: Period of the year (0-365 days) while soil-pF is less then 3.5. The standard values for mineralisation of soil organic matter, crop residues and organic manure have been determined in permanently moist soil. In this model mineralisation of organic matter is stopped when soil pF rises above 3.5.

IrrigationWater.Explanation: Amount of water available on the farm for crop production

PDeposition.Explanation: Phosphorus deposition with dust and flooding

KDeposition.Explanation: Potassium deposition with dust and flooding

MeanTemperature.Explanation: Average temperature during the moist period, when organic matter degradation is possible

ErosionAmount.Explanation: Amount of soil eroded per year

ErosionOmContent.Explanation: Percentage of organic matter in eroded soil

ErosionNContent.Explanation: Percentage of nitrogen in eroded soil

ErosionPContent.Explanation: Percentage of potassium in eroded soil

ErosionKContent.Explanation: Percentage of potassium in eroded soil

GeneralCosts.Explanation: General costs related to the farm enterprise

LabourFarmConstant.Explanation: Constant  labour required for farm maintenance

LabourHerdConstant.Explanation: Constant labour required for keeping animals

RegularLaborInput.Explanation: Regular, skilled labor that is provided by the farmer family

CasualLaborInput.Explanation: Casual, unskilled labor that is provided by the farmer family

RegularLabourAnimal.Explanation: Skilled labor that is required for this animal type

CasualLabourAnimal.Explanation: Unskilled labor that is required for this animal type

SpeciesNumber.Explanation: Number of plant species present in the field

ErosionCFactor.Explanation: Crop cover factor of the RUSLE soil loss equation

EffOrganicMatter.Explanation: Effective organic matter input by crop

WaterDemand.Explanation: Amount of water required to grow the crop to the given production level(s)

Costs.Explanation: Cost for production of the crop

Subsidies.Explanation: Subsidies for production of the crop

ScoreEffort.Explanation: Score for effort (physical) for the production activity per ha of crop or per animal

ScoreRisk.Explanation: Score for risk for the production activity per ha of crop or per animal

ScoreComplexity.Explanation: Score for complexity for the production activity per ha of crop or per animal

ScoreSatisfaction.Explanation: Score for satisfaction for the production activity per ha of crop or per animal

ToSoil.Explanation: Use as green manure, applied to the soil

FractionNonGrazPeriod.Explanation: Fraction of the amount fed to animals that is supplied during the non-grazing period (dry season/winter)

ToBedding.Explanation: Use for bedding of animals in the stable

ToHomeUse.Explanation: Use for home consumption by the farm family

ToHomeUseAPR.Explanation: Use for home consumption by the farm family

ToBurning.Explanation: Amount of dry matter burned on the field

ToFireWood.Explanation: Amount of dry matter used as fire wood

FullSelfSupply.Explanation: Indicates if the product is fully on farm produced

EnergyFireWood.Explanation: Energy contents when used as fire wood

Area.Explanation: Area of the crop in the rotation

Whereabouts.Explanation: Time spent at different sites: B|P|Y|O: B=barn, P=pasture or crop stubble, Y=open yard, O=off-farm grazing

AnimalCosts.Explanation: Costs for this animal, for breeding, veterinary care, etc.

AnmNumber.Explanation: Number of animals of this type

Production.Explanation: Average production level during the year (or the period on the farm)

BeddingSupplied.Explanation: Amount of bedding material supplied per animal per day

SaturationFactor.Explanation: Saturation value, expressed per kg body weight

StructureFactor.Explanation: Structure value, expressed per kg dry matter intake

TimeInPasture.Explanation: Time per day in pasture during grazing season

TimeInYard.Explanation: Time per day in yard during grazing season

AmountUsed.Explanation: Amount of manure used on the farm

ProducedAtSite.Explanation: Manure produced at which site on the farm (P=pasture, Y=yard or S=stable)

ProportionAtSite.Explanation: Proportion of the total manure produced at a site (pasture, yard or stable)

FractionMineralNitrogen.Explanation: Fraction of the total fertilizer N that is in inorganic form

OMContent.Explanation: Organic matter content in dry matter

FractionToSoil.Explanation: Fraction of the produced manure that is allocated for crop fertilization in the field

FractionToBiogas.Explanation: Fraction of the produced manure that is allocated for biogas production

FractionToFirewood.Explanation: Fraction of the produced manure that is allocated for use as firewood after drying for cooking and heating

FractionBeddingMaterial.Explanation: Fraction of the bedding material and feed losses that is added to this type of manure

Number.Explanation: Number present on the farm / in the household

LaborProfile.Explanation: Type in total labor hours or double click to enter labor hours month wise

OverviewDecisionVariables.Description: Overview of values of decision variables
OverviewDecisionVariables.Explanation: Overview of values of decision variables (per solution)

OverviewObjConstraints.Description: Overview of values of objectives and constraints
OverviewObjConstraints.Explanation: Overview of values of objectives and constraints (per solution)

ImportCrops.Explanation: Import of nutrients in crop products used on the farm

ImportManure.Explanation: Import of nutrients in manures and fertilizers

ExportCropProducts.Explanation: Export of nutrients in crop products from the farm

ExportAnimalProducts.Explanation: Export of nutrients in animal products from the farm

UptakeCrops.Explanation: Nutrients taken up by the growing crop and harvested in products

CropProductsToAnimals.Explanation: Nutrients from crop products supplied as feed to animals

AnimalProductsToAnimals.Explanation: Nutrients from animal products supplied as feed to animals

FeedToAnimals.Explanation: Nutrients supplied as feed to animals, both crop and animal products

AnimalIntake.Explanation: Nutrients in feeds taken up by the animals

AnimalRespiration.Explanation: Losses by respiration of animals (only carbon)

AnimalsToManure.Explanation: Nutrients in manure produced by farm animals, with added bedding material

OwnManure.Explanation: Amount of nutrients supplied to the soil in manures, including imported manures and fertilizers, after correction for losses during storage

Importmanure.Explanation: Nutrients in imported manures and fertilizers

TotalManure.Explanation: Nutrients available in the total manure

SoilLosses.Explanation: Losses of nutrients from the soil by run-off, leaching or volatilization. Calculated by difference. For carbon the degradation of soil OM and manure after application are given

Volatilization.Explanation: Gaseous losses from manures (carbon: dissimilation of carbohydrates; nitrogen: volatilization of ammonia)

Immobilization.Explanation: Net immobilization of carbon; for nitrogen the potential immobilization in the soil, dependent on the net carbon sequestration (can be subtracted from soil losses)

WaterBalance.Explanation: Percentage deviation of available water from the demand

WaterPerCrop.Explanation: Volume of water needed for cultivation of the crop at the indicated yield level

RequiredWater.Explanation: Water needed for cultivation of all crops

AvailableWater.Explanation: Water available for crop production on the farm

Digestibility.Explanation: Fraction of dry matter degraded by the animals

ExportManure.Explanation: Nutrients exported from the farm in manure

TotalLosses.Explanation: Losses of nutrients to the air (volatilization) and the soil (leaching, denitrification)

BeddingToManure.Explanation: Amount of nutrients from bedding material added to the manure

ManureBalance.Explanation: Balance between production and application of manures

TotalApplied.Explanation: Amount of manure dry matter applied to crops

GrossMarginCropsRisk.Explanation: Risk for crop gross margin on basis of historical GM and crop areas

ManurePerCrop.Explanation: Amount of manure applied to crops

ManureName.Explanation: Name of the type of manure

MarginPerHa.Explanation: Margin per unit of farm area

ReturnsPerHa.Explanation: Returns per unit of farm area

TotalActiveIngredients.Explanation: Total amount of active ingredients applied

PerCropPesticide.Explanation: Amount of pesticide applied to crops

EnergyCropResidues.Explanation: Crop Residues used for energy production

Manures.Explanation: Manures used for energy production on the farm

CropsToFermentation.Explanation: Crop products used for energy production in anaerobic fermentation

TotalEmissionCO2eq.Explanation: Summed emission expressed in CO2-equivalents from all sources

EntericCH4.Explanation: CH4 (methane) emission from fermentation processes in the rumen

ManureCH4.Explanation: CH4 (methane) emissie from excreted animal manure

ManureN2OApplied.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission from applied animal manure

ManureN2ODirect.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission from animal manure (direct emission)

ManureN2OVolatiliz.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission as a fraction of volatilized ammonia-nitrogen (indirecte emissie)

CropCH4.Explanation: Crop-specific emission for CH4 (methane), in particular for rice cultivation

ResidueEmissionCO2eq.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission from green manures or residues applied to the soil

FixationEmissionCO2eq.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission from symbiotically fixed nitrogen (by legumes)

DepositionEmissionCO2eq.Explanation: N2O (di-nitrogen-oxide) emission from atmopheric nitrogen deposition

AnimalProductImportToHousehold.Explanation: The import of animal products into the system to satisfy the nutritional needs of the household

ExportAnimalManure.Explanation: Export of manure produced by the livestock on the farm

ExportHouseholdManure.Explanation: Export of excreta produced by the household

CropProductsToManure.Explanation: Crop products added to manure, sources: feed losses, bedding material and substrate for the fermentation for biogas production

CropProductsToFermentation.Explanation: Crop products added to fermentation for biogas (energy) production

CropProductsToHousehold.Explanation: Crop products used by the household as food

AnimalProductsToHousehold.Explanation: Animal products used by the household as food

HouseholdToManure.Explanation: Excretaof the household that are added to the manure and remain within the system

HouseholdRespiration.Explanation: Respiration losses by the household members

MagnesiumRatio.Explanation: Ratio between Mg and other nutrients (Mg/(K+Na+P+Ca))

FoodGroupDemand.Explanation: Demand of food group per person

FoodGroupSupply.Explanation: Supply of food group per food

NumberHouseholdMembers.Explanation: Number of members in the household

TotalIncome.Explanation: Total income from the farm and external sources

TotalExpenditures.Explanation: Total expenditures on food and other costs

ProportionFoodCosts.Explanation: Proportion of food costs in the total expenditures

FreeBudget.Explanation: Free budget after subtraction of diet costs

FarmIncome.Explanation: Income from the activities on the farm

OffFarmIncome.Explanation: Income from activities outside the farm

FoodCosts.Explanation: Costs for food, either on-farm produced or purchased

Result.Explanation: Financial result: budget available for spending

DiversityHyperVolume.Explanation: Volume of distances in concentrations of nutrients in produced or consumed foods

FunctionalDiversity.Explanation: The functional diversity of produced or consumed foods

NutrientYield.Explanation: Number of consumer units (persons) that can be nutrished in terms of individual nutrients from the on-farm products

NutrYield.Explanation: Number of consumer units (persons) that can be nutrished in terms of individual nutrients from the on-farm products

CropBurningLoss.Explanation: Losses of nutrients upon crop burning

AnimalDensity.Explanation: Number of livestock on the farm

LivestockDensity.Explanation: Number of livestock units per unit of area

LaborHoursClasses.Description: Labor input per gender and age class
LaborHoursClasses.Explanation: Labor input per gender and age class

LaborFractionsClasses.Description: Fraction of labor per gender and age class
LaborFractionsClasses.Explanation: Fraction of labor per gender and age class

SpeciesIndices.Explanation: Indices for species richness (Margalef) and evenness (Shannon)

Efficiencies.Explanation: Efficiencies of nutrient use at farm and component levels
